subject: Onprem cluster: sustained p95 latency & 5xx spike — urgent performance review
messages:
From: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@medsafe.io>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-team@medsafe.io
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Onprem cluster: sustained p95 latency and 5xx spike

Aditya —

We're seeing a sustained regression on our on‑prem Redwood deployment since ~03:00 UTC this morning. Key symptoms: p95 latency has climbed to ~3.1s (baseline ~450ms) for text-generation routes, and 5xx responses have jumped to ~1.8% (was ~0.03%). Throughput (requests/sec) is dropping intermittently even though client QPS is flat.

We attached a short kernel log extract and a support dump (support_dump_20270520.tar.gz). Preliminary internal checks show GPU utilization dipping to 40% on affected nodes at the same time 5xx spikes start. No recent model change on our side; config pinned to model-redwood-1.

This is customer impacting (real-time feature). Can you escalate? We need an ETA for root cause and mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Lisa Gomez
CTO, MedSafe Analytics

Attachments: support_dump_20270520.tar.gz, kernel_logs_05.txt
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@medsafe.io>, ops-team@medsafe.io
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Onprem cluster: sustained p95 latency and 5xx spike

Looping engineering and CS leads —

Lisa flagged a clear production regression on the MedSafe private deployment (attached logs). Key notes from their side: p95 ~3.1s, 5xx ~1.8%, GPU util dips correlate with failures. They've pinned to model-redwood-1.

Immediate asks:
- Can infra triage for kernel-level errors / OOMs on node-03/04?
- Check KV cache warmup / eviction behavior; could cold cache + large batch combos be thrashing?
- If necessary, prepare a canary rollback to model-redwood-1-quantized or a smaller variant to stop 5xx while we fix infra.

Propose a quick triage call in 20 mins. Monica — can you own the initial investigation? Laura — please lend infra context. Marissa — FYI in case this needs sales/exec coordination.

-Aditya
Account Mgmt, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Onprem cluster: sustained p95 latency and 5xx spike

Thanks Aditya — quick guidance before triage:

1) Check kernel logs for repeated device resets / kernel OOM entries (dmesg), and NV driver errors. The log extract attached by MedSafe looks suspicious for repeated scheduling stalls.
2) Verify batch sizing and continuous batching thresholds — if batch windows grew due to throttling, token latency can spike and lead to upstream timeouts.
3) KV cache: confirm whether LRU churn increased at the same timestamps; if so, warm prefixes for the top traffic routes.
4) Prepare rollback plan: a) smaller model (redwood-1-small) on a canary instance; b) enable aggressive prefix caching; c) temporarily lower concurrency limits per connection.

Monica — take node-03 and node-04, gather: kernel dmesg, nvidia-smi samples (1s), timestamped runtime logs (runtime_trace.log), and the worker metrics bucket for last 2 hours. Start with a non-disruptive probe (no restarts) to collect steady-state metrics.

I'll be on the triage call and will coordinate if we need a released kernel patch or a configuration tweak. If a restart is required, we need customer approval for a rolling restart window.

-Laura
VP, Serving Infrastructure
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@medsafe.io>, ops-team@medsafe.io
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Onprem cluster: sustained p95 latency and 5xx spike

On Thu, May 20, 2027 at 09:40 AM Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Monica — take node-03 and node-04, gather: kernel dmesg, nvidia-smi samples (1s), timestamped runtime logs (runtime_trace.log), and the worker metrics bucket for last 2 hours.

Update from initial probe (non-disruptive):
- Found repeated device-reset messages in node-03 dmesg around 03:04–03:07 UTC; correlates with the start of p95/5xx spike.
- nvidia-smi shows GPU mem fragmentation and occasional driver timeouts on node-03; node-04 looks marginal.
- Runtime shows a flurry of failed kernel launches and slower KV cache population during the window.

Immediate mitigation I recommend:
1) Patch driver/kernel for the known nv-sched stall (we have a backport candidate that mitigates fragmentation).
2) Temporarily reduce per-worker batch limit from 32->16 and limit concurrency by 25% to reduce memory pressure.
3) Canary apply the patch on node-03 (isolated) then roll. If patch not possible within 1 hour, perform a graceful rolling restart of the worker processes to reclaim memory.

I'll stage the patch and runbook steps now — estimate 45m to canary and validate. Attaching the support dump I collected: support_dump_20270520.tar.gz

-Monica
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@medsafe.io>, Ken Park <ken.park@medsafe.io>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ops-team@medsafe.io
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: MedSafe onprem: proposed mitigation plan & maintenance window (SUP-3421)

Lisa / Ken —

Thanks for the quick flags — summary and proposed next steps:

Summary:
- Root cause signals point to GPU driver/kernel stalls on node-03 causing failed kernel launches and KV cache starvation; manifests as higher p95 (~3s) and 5xx spike (~1.8%).

Immediate mitigation (we propose):
1) Canary apply the backport kernel/driver patch to node-03 (non-disruptive to other nodes). Validate for 15–30 mins.
2) If canary looks good, roll patch across node-04..node-06 in 1–2 hour window (rolling, 1 node at a time).
3) If patch cannot be applied in the timebox, perform a rolling restart of worker processes to reclaim GPU memory and reduce fragmentation.
4) Configuration changes (temporary): reduce per-worker batch limit 32->16; lower concurrent tokens per connection by 25%; enable aggressive prefix caching for top traffic routes.

Impact: canary patch expected to restore p95 toward baseline within 10–30 mins of validation; each rolling node patch ~12–18 mins of worker restart time (no data plane reconfiguration). We will monitor and have rollback to current kernel if regression.

Requested approval: a 3‑hour maintenance window tomorrow 02:00–05:00 UTC for the rolling patch and validation. During the canary we will keep you updated every 15 mins; if we switch to rolling restart fallback we'll notify 30 mins before the first restart.

Links & ticket: SUP-3421 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-3421), runbook: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1RunbookExampleLink (runbook_v2.pdf attached).

Please confirm the requested window or propose an alternate. We can also spin up a temporary hosted fallback route if you prefer zero-touch for the maintenance window (higher latency/cost).

-Aditya
Account Mgmt, Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook_v2.pdf
